newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT--Buoyant dollar to head for new heights.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT--Buoyant dollar to head for new heights.

text.p: The U.S. dollar is set for another surge as it should continue to ride the wave of global investments drawn to U.S. financial assets, chartists said on Thursday.
The dollar rallied on Thursday as the Dow Jones vaulted above the 7700-barrier for another record high and the 30-year Treasury bond yield edged down toward 6.75 percent.

"Dollar/mark closed on a positive note, above 1.7270, the 61.8-percent retracement of the move from 1.7423, the high of June 6, to 1.7020 on Monday," said analyst Ben Morden at I.D.E.A. "We'll see some positive follow-through to 1.7330."
The dollar ended on Thursday at 1.7285/95 versus 1.7245/55 at the open and 1.7160/65 at the close on Wednesday.

Chartists said hourly charts were positive for the dollar, although an overbought situation may develop near 1.7335 marks, preventing an attack on 1.7395 resistance and then 1.7423, the top of the current range and a 39-month high.
"People tend to sell toward the high end of the range," Morden said. "Also, mark/yen is rallying and may place a slight drag on dollar/mark."
Morden pointed out that mark/yen experienced "a tremendous chart gap from 65.15 to 66.10" on Thursday.
Morden predicted mark/yen support will hold at 65.60 and the "next move may take mark/yen up to 68.00," which could cap a major dollar/mark rally.

However, dollar/mark should retain some good upside provided that 1.7215 support holds, chartists said. That level is the 62-percent retracement of the move from the 1.7423 high to 1.7080, the low on Wednesday.
Meanwhile, "dollar/yen met an objective to the downside at 110.55 and it could easily range-trade from here between 112.00 and 116.90," Morden predicted.
Dollar/yen fell on late Wednesday to a low of 110.52.
Morden described as "extremely positive" dollar/yen's late Wednesday spike to 115.70, a significant level on a "rising trendline dating back to September 1995."

Mark/Paris, a much-watched cross due to uncertainty about the European Monetary Union (EMU) suffered a worth-noting retreat of one full centime after retesting the 3.3835 level, a trendline from May 22nd that signals a possible pullback to key support at 3.3660.
Dollar/Swiss is somewhat bullish as well and ready to attack 1.4485, a 62-percent retracement from the high of 1.4625 on June 6 to the low of 1.4277 on June 9, chartists also said.
